html:
Kumtor is an open-pit gold mine high in the Tian Shan of Kyrgyzstan, at about 4,000 metres, one of the highest gold mines in the world. It began producing in 1997 and has yielded over 13 million ounces of gold, at times a tenth of the country's economy and a large share of its exports.

It was run by Centerra Gold, a Canadian company, under deals that many Kyrgyz saw as unfair. The pit cuts into glaciers to reach the ore, raising fears for water supplies. In 1998 a truck spilled nearly two tonnes of sodium cyanide into a river that flows into Lake Issyk-Kul, which led to a long dispute over the harm to villagers' health.

Kumtor became a centre of Kyrgyz politics, a test of who gets the country's wealth, and protests over it marked the years after the Tulip Revolution of 2005. In 2021 the government of Sadyr Japarov took control of the mine, and in 2022 Centerra handed it over to the state in a settlement.
